newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Sliding blue chips drag down Nigerian shares.
newsitem.headline: Sliding blue chips drag down Nigerian shares.

text.p: Nigerian shares closed lower on Tuesday, forced down by declining prices of leading stocks, traders said.
The all-share index slipped to 8683.28 from 8687.53 on Monday as First Bank and West African Portland Cement Company resumed their fall.
"Recent appreciation in the bank caused investors to take their profit. The resultant rush to sell is what is depressing the shares," one trader said.
The cement company's drop was attributed to its poor financial result announced recently.
First Bank lost 20 kobo to close at 15.00 naira while West African Portland Cement Company shed five kobo at 65.40 naira.
The two are among the top most capitalised companies in the country's stock market.
Traders said little else was done in a dull session on a wet day in Nigeria's commercial capital Lagos.
"Even an impressive first quarter result posted by a bank did not elicit any reaction from the market," one said.
FSB International Bank said its after-tax profit for the three months ended March 31, 1997 shot to 433.6 million naira from 241.7 million naira a year earlier.
The bank's shares closed unchanged at 4.07 naira.
